message.author: various Welsh traditions
message.locator: The Second Branch, Branwen sends word to her brother; local text normalized characters 420563-421266
message.excerpt: And Branwen reared a starling in the cover of the kneading trough, and she taught it to speak, and she taught the bird what manner of man her brother was. And she wrote a letter of her woes, and the despite with which she was treated, and she bound the letter to the root of the bird’s wing, and sent it towards Britain. And the bird came to this island, and one day it found Bendigeid Vran at Caer Seiont in Arvon, conferring there, and it alighted upon his shoulder and ruffled its feathers, so that the letter was seen, and they knew that the bird had been reared in a domestic manner. narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: When Efnissien learns that Branwen was married to Matholwch without his consent, he mutilates the Irish king's horses. The insult helps turn an alliance into a conflict that reaches Branwen.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Branwen's starling carries a letter across the sea after she has been mistreated and isolated. The tale makes communication a turning point in a political crisis.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read it carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: This is a Welsh tale in the Mabinogion, translated by Lady Charlotte Guest. Do not merge it with the Irish Táin Bó Cúailnge just because both are medieval Celtic-language narratives.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: Follow the chain from the wedding alliance to the insult, Branwen's message, and Bran's response; keep each step tied to the tale.

quiz.prompt: What starts the insult to Matholwch?

choices.text: Branwen refuses to send her brother a message
Matholwch takes the throne of Dyved
Efnissien mutilates his horses because the marriage was made without consulting him

quiz.explanation: The tale says Efnissien objects that his sister was married without his consent, then injures Matholwch's horses.

suggestedQuestions: What does this one text not establish?

She sends it through a merchant at the Ford
